title: Clouds
subtitle: Reading the sky
summary: Learn to name the clouds overhead, then work out why they formed and what they say about tomorrow's weather. A 22° halo round the Sun can mean rain within a day; towers at ten in the morning can mean a storm by four; a dark thin cloud will leave you dry when a deep pale one soaks you. Four branches follow the wind into the Pacific Northwest's winter rain and quiet coasts, tornadoes and hurricanes, weeks-long valley fog and hot Santa Ana winds, and the 1946 experiments that tried to make it rain with dry ice.
